description: An ORDER BY ... LIMIT page is now chosen from a segment's stored columns where it can be, and only the winners are built into result rows. That is a cost change and must never be an answer change, so these cases pin the two routes against each other on one corpus. Two cases ask for the same ordering, one at a limit above the top-K threshold where no ranking is armed and one below it where the columns choose, and the smaller page must be a prefix of the larger. The other two exercise the exclusions rather than assuming them: one carries a predicate deferred to built rows and is built so that removing that exclusion empties its answer, the other orders by a field a row view is not allowed to see. Read that difference: the first pair can only catch a column-ranked page that is wrong, never one that has silently stopped happening, which is why the exclusion case is written to fail loudly instead. Without any of this the only thing between a divergence and a shipped wrong page is that both routes call the same comparator -- true, but they feed it values from two different readers.

cases.name: the_answer_this_suite_measures_against
cases.description: Ground truth on the built path. A limit above TOPK_THRESHOLD (1000) leaves no top-K armed, so every matching row is built and sorted whole. Seven functions in this corpus exceed 150 lines, in this order by size. Every case below asks for a prefix of these.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE lines > 150 ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 1001

cases.name: a_predicate_deferred_to_built_rows_keeps_every_row_in_the_ranking
cases.description: The exclusion that stops a segment ranking its own rows while a predicate is still to run, chosen so that removing the exclusion moves this page rather than leaving it alone. A regular expression is handed to the filter over built rows unconditionally -- compiling it once for a batch beats once per row -- so it is deferred on every segment whatever columns that segment holds. `name` is not the point: a row view holds `name` and could answer an equality or a LIKE on it; what defers this predicate is the operator. The one function it matches is the third largest in a file of 32, and LIMIT 1 makes the ranking retain two per segment, so a ranking allowed to run before the predicate would keep that file's two largest functions, the predicate would then reject both, and the answer would come back empty. With the exclusion the whole file is built, filtered, and the one match survives. An earlier draft used WHERE lines > 150 here, which is answerable from a lines column and so never reached this exclusion at all, and matched too broadly to have noticed if it had.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' WHERE name MATCHES 'stream_names_desc_kind_filtered' ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 1

cases.name: the_running_trim_inside_the_column_ranked_page
cases.description: The one case here whose page is chosen from the columns. ORDER BY lines is admitted even on the many segments holding no lines column at all, because a view and the row it would build both report that field as absent and rank identically on it -- that admission is what makes the route reachable, and gating it on answerability instead left it taken by almost nothing. The candidate set is every function in the corpus. Not every segment ranks: the route also needs more matching rows in the segment than the trim's own threshold, and functions are spread thin enough that a minority of files clear it -- on the sibling workspace, 56 of 298 function-bearing files hold more than k * TOPK_OVER_FETCH = 20, which is about a fifth of the files and about half the rows. Those files pick their contribution before building it; the rest build what they matched, as before. The answer must be the same five rows in the same order as the built-path case above.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' ORDER BY lines DESC LIMIT 5

cases.name: an_ordering_the_columns_cannot_rank_still_answers
cases.description: ORDER BY usages is excluded from the column-ranked route by construction, and this case has no other disqualifier -- its one WHERE is answerable from the columns, so nothing is left to run after a row is built -- which makes the ordering field itself the reason. The per-segment usages column is a stale always-zero legacy field and the real workspace count is stamped onto a row only after it is built, so a row view is not allowed to see it at all: it reports the field absent rather than zero. A regression admitting this query to the column route would therefore rank every row equal, leaving the tie-breakers to choose which rows each file contributes before their real counts were known. These five are the most-used symbols in the corpus at 1544 uses each, so the tie-breakers order them among themselves here too; what this case pins is that they are the five, which a ranking blind to usages could only get right by accident.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE fql_kind = 'function' ORDER BY usages DESC LIMIT 5
